title: DRV Book I  -  The Lock  -  REWRITE v2 (Phase 4.1 III)

canonical_node.axiom: The argument from properties of truth to the Logos is structured in six layers plus a central claim, with each layer having a distinct epistemic status. The framework's primitive axioms are exactly three: God-as-Axiom (Axiom 1), Trinity Isomorphism (Axiom 2), and Free Will (Axiom 3). All other items are theorems, derivations, definitions, or below-floor presuppositions.
definitions: Layer 0: Properties of Truth (P0.1 - P0.7)  -  below-floor presuppositions, not axioms.
Layer 1: Gdel-Chaitin Theorem  -  external inherited result.
Layer 3: Source-Property Transmission Lemma  -  single lemma replacing four prior axioms.
Layer 5: Central Claim  -  math-moral unity, the thesis defended.
derivation: Layer 0: Seven properties of mathematical truth are observed as below-floor presuppositions.
Layer 1: Gdel-Chaitin theorem establishes the ground of mathematical truth is external to mathematics.
Layer 2: From Layer 1, the ground cannot be nothing, chaos, or deceptive.
Layer 3: Source-Property Transmission Lemma transfers Layer 0 properties plus veracity to the ground.
Layer 4: Definitions and postulates: truth is valuable, deception is wrong.
Layer 5: Central Claim: mathematical and moral truth share a single ground.
Layer 6: The ground is named Logos and identified as Axiom 1 (God-as-Axiom).
canonical_node.action: The framework should present the argument in the layered structure, with each layer's epistemic status explicit, and terminate at the Feb 14 floor without descending into divine mechanics.
boundary: Does not assert the seven properties as axioms; they are below-floor presuppositions.
Does not treat the Gdel-Chaitin theorem as an axiom of the framework.
Does not treat the Central Claim as an axiom; it is the thesis defended.
Does not exercise Axiom 2 (Trinity Isomorphism) in this series.
Does not push past the Feb 14 floor into divine mechanics.
test: Check that each layer's epistemic status is correctly labeled (below-floor, theorem, inference, lemma, definition, central claim, axiom).
Verify that the three primitive axioms are exactly as listed.
Verify that the argument terminates at the Feb 14 floor without further descent.
Verify that the Central Claim is presented as the thesis, not as an input.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a reclassified, layered argument structure that distinguishes epistemic statuses, promoting the Central Claim and Axiom 1 while demoting seven properties to below-floor presuppositions.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the content of the original twenty axioms, but reclassifies them into layers with explicit epistemic statuses, maintaining the argument's conclusion at the Feb 14 floor.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If the reclassification is removed, the framework reverts to a flat-axiom structure that misrepresents the May 10 canon, causing epistemic confusion and undermining the formal taxonomy.

overstatement_risks: Claims that the reclassification is 'load-bearing' without formal proof.
Asserts that the Gdel-Chaitin theorem 'forces everything downstream' without detailed derivation.
Treats the Central Claim as defended without presenting the full argument in this document.
kill_conditions: If the May 10 canon is not accepted as authoritative, the reclassification loses its basis.
If the Gdel-Chaitin theorem is misapplied, the argument collapses.
If the Central Claim is shown to be unsupported by Layers 0 - 4, the framework's thesis fails.
risk.lean_target: Formal verification of the reclassification against the Formal Theory v1.0 canon, and a rigorous derivation of the Gdel-Chaitin implications.

plain_summary: This document is a rewrite of Section III of 'The Lock', reclassifying the original twenty axioms into a six-layer argument structure with distinct epistemic statuses. It promotes the math-moral unity to a Central Claim and the Logos identification to Axiom 1, while demoting seven properties to below-floor presuppositions. The rewrite is internally coherent but relies on the Formal Theory v1.0 canon and does not provide formal proof of the argument's validity.
